lots.title: Planned, Preventative & Responsive Residential Property Maintenance and Compliance Services
lots.description: Measured Term Contract (JCT MTC 2024) for day-to-day maintenance, repairs, servicing, compliance works, end-of-lease works, void works and emergency callouts on residential properties in the London Borough of Bexley or surrounding areas. Portfolio scope stated in the specification: approximately 230 Council-owned street properties, 120 private leased properties managed by the Council, and 3 hostels (repairs and maintenance). Initial contract term 1 November 2026 to 31 October 2030 (4 years, fixed, no extension or price uplift).
requirements: Carry out repairs, void works and minor works, engineering repairs, and servicing and compliance works for gas and electrical installations on individual properties within the London Borough of Bexley or surrounding areas (§1 Contract Description).

Deliver general building maintenance (repairs, void works, minor works); gas servicing and safety compliance; electrical testing and servicing; fire and legionella compliance inspections; fire alarm and emergency lighting inspections to BS 5839 and the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005; 24-hour emergency out-of-hours service; pest control (EN 16636); rubbish clearance; and asbestos reports and removal (§2.3 Services).

All works shall be instructed by Order issued electronically by the Contract Administrator using a standard Works Approval Form; no work shall commence until a valid Order has been issued; variations must be agreed in writing before commencement (§3.1–3.5).

Meet response and completion time categories: Standard – within 5 working days; Urgent – same or next day and within 1 working day; Emergency – make safe within 4 hours, full completion ASAP; Small Void Works – within 10 working days; Large Void Works – within 28 working days; Emergency follow-on works to commence within 1 working day (§3.3–3.4 and §20.2 KPI 1).

Operate payment in accordance with the Housing Grants, Construction and Regeneration Act 1996 (as amended) and JCT MTC 2024 Section 4. Submit Monthly Application for Payment; invoices monthly via email within one month of valuation period; final date for payment 30 days from receipt of valid invoice; all invoices submitted within six months of Order issue; VAT shown separately (§4.1–4.6).

Comply with all applicable legislation including Building Regulations 2010 (as amended), Building Safety Act 2022 and Part 2A, CDM Regulations 2015, Gas Safety (Installation and Use) Regulations, BS 7671 IET Wiring Regulations, Fire Safety Order 2005, Environmental Protection Act 1990, and GDPR / Data Protection Act 2018 (§5.1).

Act as Principal Contractor where required under CDM 2015 and maintain an SSIP Forum registration (for example CHAS, EXOR, OHSAS) for the duration of the contract; the Authorised Officer may suspend the Works for non-compliance with health and safety obligations (§6).

Comply with the Control of Asbestos Regulations 2012; do not use asbestos-containing materials; survey premises before works; where asbestos is found or suspected, cease work and notify the Authorised Officer; removal only by specialist contractors appointed by the Council (§6 Asbestos).

Use portable electrical equipment at no greater than 110v, double-insulated or effectively earthed, leads properly terminated, clamped and insulated, all compliant with the Electricity at Work Regulations 1989 and PUWER 1998 (§6).

Provide safe working method statements and generic risk assessments for hot works and for work at height; comply with Working at Height Regulations 2005 and the Council's scaffolding protocol; obtain a Permit to Work for hot works (§6).

Operate COSHH (Control of Substances Hazardous to Health Regulations 2002) controls on site, with written COSHH assessments available, and supply PPE under the Personal Protective Equipment at Work Regulations 2002 including safety headgear, protective gloves, footwear and high-visibility jackets; eye protection to BS 7028:1999 (§6).
Report accidents, incidents and dangerous occurrences to the Authorised Officer and HSE under RIDDOR 2013 (§6).

Comply with Building Regulations and the Workplace (Health, Safety and Welfare) Regulations 1992 for glazing; all safety glazing clearly and permanently marked to BS 6206:1981, BS 952-1:1995 Parts 1 & 2, and BS 6262:2005 Part 4 (§6).

Protect, uphold and maintain services (gas, water, electricity, telecoms, sewers) during works; locate services before excavation; make good any damage at Contractor's expense; compensate for interference or dislocation to public or private services (§7.4–7.5).

Carry out works without danger or loss of security to users; minimise disruption, noise and dust; keep facilities (light, power, heat, drinking water, sanitation) operational for occupants or provide approved temporary services; remove ladders and platforms at end of each working day or store in a lockable store; keep fire escape routes clear (§9 Premises Protocols).

Attend residential premises only by prior appointment; leave a calling card if access is not given; treat clients in a non-discriminatory manner; maintain confidentiality; follow a no-smoking policy; ensure safeguarding standards and never attend unannounced (§9, §12.2, §12.3).

Carry out all electrical works in accordance with BS 7671 (IET Wiring Regulations) and provide an electrical installation certificate compliant with Part P of the Building Regulations for all new circuits on completion (§9).

Undertake an annual comprehensive service of every gas appliance and system to manufacturers' specification; prepare service reports and landlords' gas safety records (LGSR) for each dwelling; provide monthly submission of LGSR information to the Client Gas Contract Team (§10.1).

Conduct full annual gas safety inspections to the current Gas Safety (Installation and Use) Regulations covering internal gas supplies, fitted gas appliances, flues and terminals, and ventilation; issue landlords' gas safety report (§10.2).

Conduct void gas safety inspections including fitting a meter blanking disc after a tightness test, capping/plugging off internal gas supplies and disconnecting and cap/plugging off fitted gas appliances; issue LGSR (§10.3).

Provide a comprehensive 24-hour breakdown service for the contract term and execute system boiler replacements following survey and prior approval, ensuring no property is left without hot water or domestic water services for more than 24 hours (§10.4–10.5).

Ensure all operatives hold valid CSCS cards, appropriate trade qualifications, photo ID and an enhanced Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check; register operatives on Gas Safe for gas work and as Registered Competent Persons or Registered Third-Party Certifiers for electrical works (§11, §12.1).

Use British Standards or equivalent for goods, materials and workmanship; do not use second-hand materials or equipment; install all items in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions and supplied components (§11, §9).

Provide visible, photo identification cards for all staff including photo, name, trade (with 'Trainee' where appropriate), contractor name and address, contact number and expiry date no more than 1 year from issue (§11).

Operate in accordance with environmental and sustainability principles: promote recycling, reduce waste, use sustainable materials, dispose of waste lawfully under the Environmental Protection Act 1990, carry spill kits, and retain Waste Disposal Certificates (§13).
Provide free-of-charge quotation visits when requested by Council officers to determine required works (§14).

Provide 12-month warranty on repairs and installations; rectify defective work within 4 days of notification; ensure no additional cost to the Council other than spare parts; complete warranty cards on behalf of clients (§16).

Maintain communication with the Council: answerphone not acceptable during normal hours; supervisors and representatives equipped with mobile phones; maintain out-of-hours emergency contact Monday–Friday 07:00–09:00 and 18:00–24:00, Saturday and Sunday 08:00–12:00 (§20 Communication).
Comply with the Transfer of Undertakings (Protection of Employment) Regulations 2006 (TUPE) in respect of staff from the existing contractors who will transfer to the successful contractor (§21).

evaluation_criteria.criterion: KPI 1 – Repair Response & Completion Times (Service Performance)
evaluation_criteria.summary: Minimum service levels for repair response and completion: Standard within 5 working days; Urgent within 1 working day; Emergency make safe within 4 hours with full completion ASAP; Small Void Works within 10 working days; Large Void Works within 28 working days. Measured monthly using job completion data from the Client's or Contractor's CAFM / works order log.
evaluation_criteria.weighting_text: Minimum 90% compliance across all repair categories, measured monthly.

evidence_anchor.anchor_text: KPI 1 – Repair Response & Completion Times (Service Performance) ... A minimum of 90% compliance across all repair categories measured monthly.

evaluation_criteria.criterion: KPI 2 – Statutory Compliance & Property Safety (Zero Tolerance KPI)
evaluation_criteria.summary: Contractor shall ensure 100% statutory compliance at all times across the Bexley-owned temporary accommodation housing stock, including Annual Gas Safety Certification (CP12), Electrical Safety Reports (EICR) and Energy Performance Certification (EPC). Measurement by monthly compliance reporting with real-time updates and visibility via dashboard or spreadsheet.

evidence_anchor.anchor_text: KPI 2 – Statutory Compliance & Property Safety (Zero Tolerance KPI) ... 100% compliance (zero tolerance).

evaluation_criteria.criterion: KPI 3 – Void Turnaround & Property Readiness (Critical TA KPI)
evaluation_criteria.summary: Contractor shall return void properties to a fully lettable standard within 10 days for small voids and 28 days for large voids, inclusive of all repairs, compliance checks and certification. Measured from handover date to certification of lettable status.

evidence_anchor.anchor_text: KPI 3 – Void Turnaround & Property Readiness (Critical TA KPI) ... A minimum of 90% compliance measured monthly.

This is a services contract (residential property maintenance). Product requirement seeds represent tooling / PPE / consumables / administrative items that the contractor must use or provide (e.g. 110V portable electrical equipment, PPE kit, spill kits, meter blanking discs, ID cards, uPVC trunking, safety glazing, fire alarm / emergency lighting inspection packages). They are indirect demand signals rather than core goods being procured, so downstream candidate generation should treat them as low-priority seeds unless reinforced by a pricing schedule or bill of quantities.

evidence_anchors.anchor_text: CONTRACT SPECIFICATION – Measured Term Contract – Planned, Preventative & Responsive Residential Property Maintenance and Compliance Services
This Contract is for: Carrying out Repairs, Void works and Minor Works; Engineering Repairs; Servicing and Compliance Works for Gas and Electrical Installations
This Contract shall be governed by the JCT Measured Term Contract 2024 (MTC 2024)
230 Council-owned street properties; 120 private leased properties managed by the Council; 3 Hostels

Services include: General building maintenance; Gas servicing and safety compliance; Electrical testing and servicing; Fire and Legionella compliance inspections; Fire alarms and Emergency Lighting inspection by a competent person, according to BS 5839 standards and the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005; 24-hour emergency out-of-hours service; Pest Control service in accordance with E.N 16636; Rubbish Clearance; Asbestos reports and removal

Priority and Response Time: Standard within 5 working days; Urgent same or next day and within 1 working day; Emergency make safe within 4 hours, full completion ASAP; Small Void Works within 10 working days; Large Void Works within 28 working days
Payment shall operate fully in accordance with: Housing Grants, Construction and Regeneration Act 1996 (as amended); JCT MTC 2024 Section 4.

The Contractor shall comply with all applicable legislation, including: Building Regulations 2010 (as amended); Building Safety Act 2022 and Part 2A; CDM Regulations 2015; Gas Safety (Installation and Use) Regulations; BS 7671 – IET Wiring Regulations; Fire Safety Order 2005; Environmental Protection Act 1990; GDPR / Data Protection Act 2018

Control of Asbestos Regulations 2012 (CAR 2012); BS 6206:1981 Safety Glazing Specification; BS 952-1:1995 Parts 1 & 2; BS 6262:2005 Part 4; BS 7028:1999 Eye Protection; Electricity at Work Regulations 1989; PUWER 1998; Working at Height Regulations 2005; COSHH 2002; PPE at Work Regulations 2002; RIDDOR 2013; SSIP (CHAS, EXOR, OHSAS)
Gas Safety (Installation and Use) Regulations 1998 and BS 7671:200 Requirement for Electrical Installations - IET Wiring Regulations Eighteenth Edition

All electrical works must be carried out in accordance with current I.E.T wiring Regulations, (BS7671). ... electrical installation certificate complaint with Part P of the current Building Regulations for all new circuits on completion of works.
An annual comprehensive service of every gas appliance and system to the manufacturers' specification ... service reports and landlords gas safety record (LGSR)
Carry out an full annual gas safety inspection to comply with the current Gas Safety (Installation and Use) Regulations.
The gas meter is to be fitted with a meter blanking disc after a tightness test has been carried out.
System Boiler Replacements ... no property shall be left without hot water or other domestic water services for any period greater than 24 hours.

Gas Safe for work involving gas or gas appliances, Registered Competent Persons or Registered Third-Party Certifiers for work on electrical installations; Construction Skills Certification Scheme; photographic identification card
Hold enhanced Disclosure and barring service (DBS)

The Contractor's attention is drawn to the provisions of The Environmental Protection Act 1990 (EPA1990) with regard to the disposal of waste ... Contractors should carry and have access to 'spill kits' on their vehicles.
Equipment defects and/or breakdowns occurring within twelve months of repair or installation shall be rectified by the contractor at no extra cost to the Council, other than the cost of spare parts.
The contract will be awarded on a fixed term basis for four years from 1 st November 2026 to 31st October 2030 with no option to extend or price uplifts.
KPI 1 – Repair Response & Completion Times ... A minimum of 90% compliance across all repair categories measured monthly.

KPI 2 – Statutory Compliance & Property Safety (Zero Tolerance KPI) ... Annual Gas Safety Certification (CP12); Electrical Safety Reports (EICR); Energy Performance certification (EPC) ... 100% compliance (zero tolerance).
KPI 3 – Void Turnaround & Property Readiness (Critical TA KPI) ... small voids within 10 days and 28 days for a large voids ... A minimum of 90% compliance measured monthly.
Transfer of Undertakings (Protection of Employment) Regulations 2006
